correctness.rationale: The edge-product map from vertex torus onto H:{∏odd u_i=∏even u_i} has each fiber of size Q. For r-dimensional coefficient space W, simultaneous zero coordinates correspond to U=W^⊥ of dimension d, giving Q|U∩H|≤Q^{d+1} by an injective choice of d coordinate functionals. Balanced odd/even blocks attain equality for d≤k. If equality holds, each coordinate linear functional of U must be nowhere zero on the full parameter torus; q>2 forces support on exactly one parameter variable. The full torus H constraint is equivalent to occupancy differences divisible by Q and a single scalar-product equation. Modding out d free block scalings yields Q^{2k−d−1} planes per unlabeled partition. Independent enumerations of balanced/residue block partitions produced q=5 six-cycle minimizers 256,576,96 for d=1,2,3 and q=3 six-cycle d=3 minimizers 60. The code’s included verification script treats the q=5,d=3 construction as nonexhaustive; global optimality relies on proof, not that construction.

value.rationale: Natural higher-dimensional support invariants and a complete extremal-subspace classification for a sparse toric code family whose ordinary weight enumerator is already known. The exact congruence-balanced partition phase across field sizes is a mathematically motivated nontrivial refinement. The half-dimensional threshold and full r≥k hierarchy can inform higher-support geometric and coding questions, without requiring a downstream general theorem.

final_claim: For the affine-torus evaluation code of the 2k-cycle with k≥3 and q>2, its generalized weights for k≤r<2k are (q−1)^{2k}−(q−1)^{2k−r+1}, with d_{2k}=(q−1)^{2k}; all minimizing r-subcodes are counted by Q^{2k−d−1} times the number of d-block partitions of edge indices whose odd/even occupancy differences vanish modulo Q=q−1, d=2k−r.
limitations: No exact claim for generalized weights 1≤r<k and no full distribution away from minimizing subcodes.
